title: More Tricks
intro: The ones that did not fit anywhere else: templates, key commands, project hygiene, bouncing and the small habits that quietly save hours.

tips.t: Open Key Commands with ⌥K and use the search box
tips.d: Open Key Commands with ⌥K, type a term in the search field to find a command by name, then assign a key to it.

src.label: Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Save your key commands as a set and back it up
tips.d: In the Key Commands window (⌥K), click the Actions button, choose Save As, name the set and click Save. That captures your whole set of custom shortcuts, including any Touch Bar assignments. Keep a copy of the file somewhere safe; losing a year of custom shortcuts to a reinstall is entirely avoidable.

src.label: Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Save your go-to plug-in chains as channel strip settings
tips.d: Set up a channel strip with the plug-ins you reach for most, then click the Setting button at the top of the channel strip and choose Save Channel Strip Setting as. A channel strip setting stores the plug-ins and their settings, so choosing it later from the same Setting pop-up menu brings back the whole chain at once.

src.label: Apple — Work with channel strip settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Put your key commands on the Touch Bar or a controller button
tips.d: In the Key Commands window, select a command, click Learn by Touch Bar, tap a Touch Bar button and give it a name. It then appears on the Touch Bar's Keyboard Shortcuts screen. For hardware, select the command (use the Search field) and press a button on your control surface. Its name appears in the Assignments field.

src.label: Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Assign controller buttons to key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Build separate templates for writing, mixing and mastering
tips.d: A writing template loads instantly with a handful of instruments. A mixing template has your buses and reference chain. They are different jobs and they deserve different starting points.

tips.t: Use Project Alternatives instead of Save As
tips.d: File > Project Alternatives > New Alternative keeps every version inside one project. Apple's guide says alternatives are "saved as part of the project and share the same assets", so you are not duplicating gigabytes of recordings to try a different arrangement.

src.label: Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Keep a reference track in every project, muted at the top
tips.d: A commercial track at the top of the session, routed to the master, muted. Unmute it whenever you lose perspective — which will be every hour.

tips.t: Name your bounce files with the date
tips.d: “Mix_v3.wav” tells you nothing in six weeks. “Song_2026‑04‑18_mix3.wav” tells you everything.

tips.t: ⌘B bounces the project or the current section
tips.d: Choose File > Bounce > Project or Section, or press ⌘B. With Cycle mode off and no regions selected, Logic bounces the whole project. With Cycle on, the bounce range matches the locators; with regions selected, it matches the selection. You can also set it with the Start and End value sliders. Select more than one destination file type to bounce several formats in one pass.

src.label: Apple — Set the bounce range in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Check the Normalize setting before you bounce
tips.d: Both the project bounce and Bounce Regions in Place have a Normalize setting. Off leaves the level alone. Overload Protection Only turns the level down only where it would clip above 0 dB. On raises the level so the highest peak reaches the maximum possible without clipping.

src.label: Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Bounce offline unless external MIDI or inputs are involved
tips.d: Offline bouncing is typically faster than realtime. But only internal sources — audio and software instrument tracks — can bounce offline, not MIDI tracks or audio channel inputs. External MIDI sound sources routed to the Mixer through aux channels need Realtime. If you're unsure, choose Automatic and Logic decides, based on whether channels have plug-ins that need a realtime bounce.

src.label: Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Leave room for tails at the end of the bounce range
tips.d: To leave room for reverb and delay tails, push the End position past the last note with the End value slider in the Bounce dialog before you bounce. With Cycle mode on, you can drag the right locator instead, because the bounce range matches the locators. Then listen to the end of the file before you send it.

src.label: Apple — Set the bounce range in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Colour and name everything before you leave the session
tips.d: Five minutes at the end of a session saves twenty at the start of the next one.

tips.t: Save a version before every major change
tips.d: New Alternative, then experiment freely. Fear of breaking something is the biggest brake on creative decisions.
